video_title: Lucas Schuermann - Swapping Out Perpetual Futures (S7E34)
gist: Variational co-founder Lucas Schuermann argues onchain derivatives will migrate from central-limit order books to a single-dealer RFQ principal-brokerage model (its internal OOLP), because flow segmentation and internalization let one dealer quote retail tighter than a fee-charging exchange. The larger structural bet is on the instrument itself: rather than bootstrapping crypto order-book depth for real-world assets, Variational hedges directly into TradFi dealers and is replacing perpetual futures with cash-settled total-return-style 'swaps' carrying a flat SOFR-plus financing leg (~4.5-5% vs the 7-10% perp funding equilibrium), backed by over $1 billion of signed dealer open-interest capacity.

themes.theme: RFQ Single-Dealer Model vs Order Books

insights.claim: Variational's retail platform Omni charges zero maker and taker fees and monetizes entirely in the spread, betting that its all-in cost still beats venues charging fees on top of their spread.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: If all-in execution cost rather than headline fees becomes the competitive axis onchain, fee-based exchange revenue models face compression; watch whether zero-fee RFQ venues take share from CLOB perp DEXs.
insights.quote: Our execution costs are some of the best anywhere on Omni because we have zero fees plus very tight spreads, but we expect those to actually improve over time, mostly due to the economy of scale here.

insights.claim: The structural advantage in Variational's model is not RFQ-versus-order-book matching but that a single internal principal (OOLP) takes the other side of every trade with full information about the counterparty, size and direction up front.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Frames RFQ as a marketing wrapper and single-dealer principal brokerage as the real moat, a test for any 'RFQ DEX' pitch that lacks a balance-sheet principal behind it.
insights.quote: RFQ versus orderbook is a bit of a semantic way in which we do that matching. The bigger difference is actually again we're on the other side of the trade.

insights.claim: Flow segmentation is the mechanical reason a single-dealer venue can quote tighter than an order book: publicly posted quotes must be priced defensively against being sniped or front-run by anonymous high-frequency takers, while a known-retail RFQ can be priced as non-toxic.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Explains why segmented retail flow is structurally worth more than anonymous flow, and why platforms that can prove non-toxicity should win on price.
insights.quote: we don't have to be taking down floor or posting quotes that can be sniped by anyone that can be frontr run by high frequency tra takers

insights.claim: A market maker's spread is a decreasing function of scale, because scale lowers exchange fee tiers, improves connectivity, raises internalization rates and sharpens short-term alpha, which is why firms like Jane Street and Jump earn billions per quarter while still quoting tight.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Implies onchain market making is a winner-take-most, scale-driven business where early volume leadership compounds into a durable pricing edge.
insights.quote: The bigger the economy of scale, the cheaper they can be because the lower their fee tiers are, the better connectivity they have, the more internalization they have, the better short-term alpha they have

insights.claim: Variational explicitly does not B-book or counter-trade users; it hedges and positions itself as an aggregator optimizing for best all-in price rather than a market maker maximizing profit per dollar traded.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Distinguishes the model from CFD shops that profit from client losses, a key diligence question for any single-dealer onchain venue.
insights.quote: We don't counter trade users. We don't Vbook

insights.claim: Variational does not yet offer an API and plans to add one, intending to service retail-style algorithmic clients while using detection, quote widening and speed bumps to deter a small number of tier-one HFT arbitrageurs on an individual basis.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: API launch is a discrete catalyst for volume growth but also the main vector for adverse selection; watch whether spreads widen after it ships.
insights.quote: we don't have an API yet. It's on the road map.

insights.claim: Hoffstein's challenge is that if broker-like platforms absorb non-toxic retail flow, the residual flow left on public venues becomes more toxic, spreads there widen, and the aggregator's own hedging footprint becomes structurally more expensive.
insights.speaker: Corey Hoffstein
insights.so_what: The key bear case for RFQ aggregators: their own success could degrade the venues they depend on to lay off risk.

insights.claim: Schuermann argues the opposite, that if non-toxic flow becomes scarce and concentrated in one aggregator, that aggregator gains negotiating power with hedging venues because even its residual hedging flow is desirable relative to the toxic flow those venues otherwise see.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Reframes flow scarcity as pricing power rather than a cost problem; a template for assessing any intermediary that concentrates benign order flow.
insights.quote: If everyone else's flow is toxic and ours is not, that's the good thing.

insights.claim: Schuermann expects a thinning of the herd among crypto venues, with fewer price-discovery exchanges surviving as infrastructure while retail flow migrates to broker-like platforms, mirroring the traditional split between exchanges and brokerages.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Bearish for the long tail of perp DEXs and exchange tokens that assume permanent retail flow; bullish for whoever captures the broker layer.
insights.quote: exchanges are infrastructure. They are for order matching. They are for price discovery. They are for institutions hedging against each other in HFT. I do think eventually retail flow will move to a broker-like model like ours.

themes.theme: The TradFi Liquidity Gap in Onchain RWAs

insights.claim: Real-world-asset perpetuals went from a niche gold-perp product to exploding in depth, volume and open interest over the past twelve months, with most venues listing them by having external market makers quote an onchain book while hedging in markets that are offchain and sometimes closed.
insights.speaker: Corey Hoffstein
insights.so_what: Identifies the structural fragility in the fastest-growing onchain product category: hedge availability does not match trading hours.

insights.claim: The depth gap between traditional markets and crypto order books is measured in orders of magnitude, with TradFi trading single-digit to double-digit trillions a day versus crypto venues trading a few hundred million.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Quantifies why RWA perps priced off crypto-native liquidity carry hidden execution and gap risk relative to their TradFi equivalents.
insights.quote: We're talking about markets that trade singledigit and sometimes even double digit trillions a day versus markets that trade a few hundred million.

insights.claim: Only roughly 30 to 50 assets are genuinely tradable with decent depth at retail size onchain today, versus thousands to tens of thousands of global markets in traditional finance where a prop trader with a $10-20 million book barely thinks about execution.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Sets the listings gap any onchain RWA platform must close, and flags that most already-listed onchain RWAs carry laughably wide spreads.
insights.quote: they're listed, but the spreads are laughably wide

insights.claim: Variational's answer to the liquidity gap is to skip rebuilding order books entirely and connect directly to the largest TradFi dealers and non-bank and prospective bank prime brokerages, making its onchain liquidity approximately equivalent to TradFi liquidity.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: The central bet of the business; if dealer connectivity holds, onchain RWA listings can go from dozens to thousands without incentive spend.
insights.quote: We just skip the queue. It's that simple. We're not rebuilding liquidity. We're aggregating.

insights.claim: Schuermann draws a sharp distinction between connecting to dealers, where pricing actually originates, and connecting to brokers or to crypto-native market makers holding proxied TradFi liquidity through a retail broker.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: A diligence test for competing RWA venues: ask whether their TradFi liquidity is dealer-direct or proxied through retail brokerage rails.
insights.quote: I would not describe our connectivity as to brokers. I'd describe it to dealers because that's where the pricing sources is actually coming from.

insights.claim: Hedging RWA flow onchain only makes sense during off-hours and weekends where crypto has genuine 24/7 product-market fit, or during pricing-band dislocations, and is otherwise an explicit no during normal market hours.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Defines the narrow and shrinking window in which onchain RWA liquidity has a real edge over TradFi venues.

insights.claim: Crypto's 24/7 advantage in RWAs is transient because traditional finance is itself moving toward continuous trading across inter-dealer networks, primes and exchanges, including CME listing additional single stocks.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: If TradFi goes 24/7, the main differentiator of crypto RWA perps evaporates, a direct risk to platforms whose moat is weekend coverage.
insights.quote: traditional finance itself is rocketing towards 24x7 trading

themes.theme: Perpetual Futures: Funding, Roll and Index Design Flaws

insights.claim: Variational holds roughly 12-13% of crypto RWA perpetual open interest share versus Hyperliquid at over 70% and most other platforms at 1-2%, achieved without an order book.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: A concrete market-share benchmark for tracking whether the aggregator model is taking share from CLOB perp DEXs in RWAs.
insights.quote: I think we're at 12 or 13% of RWBA open interest in crypto on the crypto pers by open interest share. Hyperlquid I think is at 70 plus. Most of the rest of the guys are at like 1 to 2%.

insights.claim: Perpetual futures are not fungible across venues because funding rates are variable and index price, mark price and roll-schedule definitions all differ, which is the core quant problem an aggregator must solve to hedge across venues.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Explains why cross-venue perp aggregation is hard and defensible, and why instrument-spec alignment is worth more than raw connectivity.
insights.quote: funding rates are variable. The definition of index and mark prices are different.

insights.claim: Variational's oil, copper and natural gas perps reference dated futures with a blended five-day roll cycle, forcing the platform to set a funding rate compensating for predictable roll-driven price drift without an order book to do it organically.
insights.speaker: Corey Hoffstein
insights.so_what: Roll-driven carry is an underappreciated hidden cost in commodity perps; traders should model it explicitly rather than assume spot tracking.

insights.claim: Index construction diverges by asset class when underlying markets close: equities freeze at the last value over weekends while commodities switch to a price derived from the platform's own book, with exponential weighted moving averages used to smooth overnight prices.
insights.speaker: Corey Hoffstein
insights.so_what: Weekend index modes determine liquidation risk on RWA perps; a mispriced weekend index is where retail gets hurt.

insights.claim: Early generations of weekend-traded synthetic perps produced funding rates in the thousands and tens of thousands of percent, and in some observed cases traders deliberately pushed prices around to exploit that mechanism.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Historical evidence that weekend synthetic indices are gameable, a live risk for any platform listing RWA perps over closed-market periods.
insights.quote: we'd see funding rates go to thousands and tens of thousands of percent over the weekend and sometimes this was an intentional trading strategy by some individuals that we saw

insights.claim: The unpredictability of perp funding and basis is the problem nobody in crypto talks about, and it undermines the original appeal of perps as the simple, one-click, delta-one leveraged instrument.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: If funding unpredictability is the binding constraint on holding periods, the market is underpricing demand for a fixed-carry alternative.
insights.quote: This is the problem that no one talks about with per and I think it's actually a big problem that we shouldn't ignore especially for retail traders the complexity and unpredictability of the funding rate of the basis.

insights.claim: Most RWA perp platforms do not pass dividends through to holders, which erodes the case for holding a levered synthetic over the underlying across multi-week horizons.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: A concrete, checkable cost line that makes long-horizon RWA perp exposure worse than it looks on a price chart.
insights.quote: a lot of these platforms don't even pay me dividends

insights.claim: Variational's new instrument is a cash-settled swap with a price-return leg plus an explicit financing leg, closest to an institutional total return swap, designed to approximate the underlying's return as exactly as possible including passing through dividends, cash flows and corporate actions.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Creates a new onchain product category; if it takes share it changes what delta-one onchain exposure means and which venues can offer it.

insights.claim: Swaps solve two problems at once: they remove funding-rate variability for the user and align the onchain instrument spec with TradFi derivatives so the platform can hedge directly without pricing in basis conversions.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Instrument alignment is the mechanism that unlocks TradFi-depth liquidity onchain, the causal link investors should test.
insights.quote: We're solving the problem primarily of funding rate and secondarily of being able to hedge directly against trady derivatives.

insights.claim: Schuermann claims swaps are strictly better than perps in almost every respect, offering predictability instead of funding variability plus a materially cheaper cost of carry.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: A direct challenge to the perp as crypto's dominant leveraged instrument, and the boldest falsifiable claim in the conversation.
insights.quote: I would go so far as to say that solves in almost every respect as a superset meaning strictly better than a perk.

insights.claim: The swap financing leg is expected to price around SOFR plus 100 basis points, roughly a 4.5 to 5% annualized cost of carry, versus the 7-8-10% per annum equilibrium typically seen in perp funding.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: A roughly 300-500bp annual carry saving on levered delta-one exposure, the single most quantifiable takeaway in the episode.
insights.quote: In many cases, this spread to sofur, in other words, the USD borrow rate is going to be substantially lower than what we usually see as the equilibrium rate set for per like more in the 7 to 8 to 10% peranom. This is probably going to be in that 4.5 to 5% range.

insights.claim: Because a CFD or total return swap always trades against a dealer writing the other side, the instrument cannot be listed on an order book at all, which Schuermann treats as the structural reason competitors cannot replicate it.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: If correct, the instrument itself is the moat rather than the technology, and CLOB-based competitors are architecturally excluded.
insights.quote: This isn't something you can do on an order boat.

insights.claim: The swap financing leg is flat and predictable but not fixed for an indefinite term; it floats as a spread to SOFR driven mainly by US Fed policy, analogous to how a bank account rate moves with monetary policy rather than daily market rates.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Traders should model these swaps as floating-rate financing with policy-rate duration, not as a locked-in term trade.

insights.claim: Variational will list both perps and swaps side by side near-term, with perps retained only for traders who specifically want exposure to the funding rate itself or who need 24/7 trading, since swaps trade traditional market hours by definition.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Defines the residual use case for perps, namely funding-rate basis trades and weekend coverage, both of which Schuermann expects to shrink.
insights.quote: Users should trade per if they specifically want exposure to the funding rate or in the near- term if they want the ability to trade at 24 by7.

insights.claim: Schuermann expects the weekend-trading rationale for perps to rapidly diminish as an as-yet-untimed phase three extends swaps beyond closed market hours, opening a path to merging the two instrument definitions or steering most flow into swaps.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: A phase-three 24/7 swap launch would be the event that makes the perp obsolete on this platform, a catalyst to watch.
insights.quote: I don't want to publicly commit that we would be sunsetting per se, but I think there is a world in which we eventually look to kind of merge these definitions

themes.theme: Financing Spreads, Dealer Capacity and Balance-Sheet Moat

insights.claim: Hoffstein was quoted SOFR plus 100 on single-name US equity total return swaps in January and closer to SOFR plus 300 more recently, a roughly 200bp intra-year widening driven by bank balance-sheet availability.
insights.speaker: Corey Hoffstein
insights.so_what: Direct evidence that single-name TRS financing is repricing sharply, relevant to anyone using swap financing or levered single-name exposure.
insights.quote: got quoted on some names sofur plus 100. More recently getting quoted on those same names it was closer to sofur plus 300.

insights.claim: Hoffstein attributes the TRS financing widening to bank balance-sheet constraints around the SpaceX IPO combined with surging demand for leverage from levered ETFs in popular single names.
insights.speaker: Corey Hoffstein
insights.so_what: Identifies levered ETF growth and large IPO underwriting as competing claims on the same dealer balance sheet, a cost driver for anyone financing equity exposure.
insights.quote: what was happening with especially around the SpaceX IPO with banks and then we just have seen this huge demand for leverage in the US with levered ETFs particularly in some of these single names

insights.claim: Schuermann expects Variational's swap financing to be more stable than the SOFR+100 to SOFR+300 swing an individual investor experiences, because financing spreads are markups on balance-sheet availability and scale counterparties like Bridgewater or Millennium negotiate both lower and flatter terms with their primes.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Financing-spread volatility is a function of counterparty size, so aggregating retail into one large counterparty is itself a source of carry alpha.
insights.quote: there's a big difference between you and the quotes you might receive at sofa plus 100 or plus 300 versus Bridgewater or Millennium versus their prime

insights.claim: Variational has signed over $1 billion of open interest capacity with TradFi dealers as a first tranche of commercial agreements, with more in discussion to cover more assets and additional global markets.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: A hard, verifiable capacity number that bounds how large the swap product can scale in the near term.
insights.quote: funnily enough, a billion dollars is just us getting started. This is a first trunch of commercial agreements we did with some early partners.

insights.claim: Schuermann reads dealers' willingness to commit over $1 billion of capacity to an unreleased, unproven product category as evidence those partners expect swaps to displace perps quickly.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Dealer capital commitment is third-party validation worth more than platform marketing; track whether that capacity actually gets drawn.
insights.quote: It shows the faith that these partners have that swaps are really going to take over and replace per very quickly.

insights.claim: TradFi hedging capacity will be directed primarily at swaps rather than perps, with TradFi liquidity used only sparingly to supplement perps in what Variational calls phase 1.5, because the aligned instrument delivers the biggest user-experience gain per unit of scarce capacity.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Internal capital allocation is a tell: scarce dealer capacity flowing to swaps signals where management expects volume to migrate.

insights.claim: Variational does not rehypothecate user balances, isolating them in independent smart contracts described as settlement or escrow pools, with a fully separate OOLP balance sheet collateralizing positions.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Removes a common failure mode in crypto intermediaries, but also means growth is capped by firm capital rather than user float.
insights.quote: We do not rehyperate user balances.

insights.claim: Schuermann treats balance sheet and dealer access as the primary moat, arguing competitors cannot easily obtain billions in open interest capacity or even connect to these dealers in the first place, particularly since swaps do not trade on exchanges.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: If the moat is relationships and capital rather than code, it is not forkable, which is unusual for an onchain protocol.
insights.quote: it's not trivial to access billions of dollars in open interest capacity with dealers. I mean it's not trivial or I would argue possible at all for our competitors to connect to these guys in the first place.

insights.claim: Variational currently has roughly $500 million of RWA perp open interest and about $1.5 billion on the platform as a whole, with Schuermann expecting much of the RWA perp book to migrate into swaps near-term.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Baseline metrics to benchmark the migration: the RWA perp to swap open-interest mix is the clearest proof point for the thesis.
insights.quote: We have 500 million in RWA per right now. I foresee a lot of that moving towards swaps in the near term. We have 1.5 billion on our platform as a whole.

insights.claim: Schuermann sizes the addressable onchain derivatives market at roughly $10 billion or more of open interest today and argues many multiples of that are attainable if benchmarked against retail brokerages globally.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Frames the TAM comparison as brokerage rather than crypto exchange, implying a far larger ceiling if the analogy holds.
insights.quote: the onchain space probably has around 10 billion or beyond of open interest that we should be addressing

insights.claim: Schuermann holds the view that onchain real-world-asset exposure will eventually exceed all cumulative crypto exposure onchain.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: The macro premise underwriting the entire strategy; if RWAs dominate onchain volume, infrastructure built purely for crypto-native assets is mispriced.

themes.theme: Institutional Pro Platform and Democratized Access

insights.claim: The benefit of onchain swaps accrues less to the largest US institutions, who already face Morgan Stanley Prime and can trade any delta-one OTC product, than to mid-pack hedge funds, prop shops and family offices in Asia and elsewhere that struggle to get an ISDA done with a tier-one prime.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Identifies the genuinely underserved segment for onchain delta-one as mid-tier and non-US institutions rather than retail alone.
insights.quote: if you're the biggest of the big Millennium or Citadel and so on facing Morgan Stanley Prime yeah you have access to absolutely everything we're doing and beyond if you're retail absolutely not

insights.claim: Schuermann flags non-financial corporates as an untapped and mispriced user base, since a Southeast Asian corporate hedging cross-currency or oil exposure needs predictable cost of carry and a familiar instrument, not a crypto-native perp with variable basis.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: A non-obvious second-order market: corporate hedging demand onchain requires fixed-carry instruments, which only the swap structure provides.
insights.quote: that's a fascinating use case of these instruments that I think is not well priced

insights.claim: The institutional Pro platform is a different value proposition entirely: a multi-dealer venue handling the full life cycle of trading, settlement and clearing for nonlinear OTC products such as options and structured products, not liquidity aggregation.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Separates two businesses often conflated in the pitch: single-dealer retail aggregation versus multi-dealer institutional clearing infrastructure.

insights.claim: Schuermann characterizes current institutional crypto OTC workflow as laughably antiquated, with quotes obtained by phone, price discovery on Telegram, fees paid to intermediating agents, and operations teams moving funds against email confirmations.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Quantifies the operational friction onchain settlement would remove, the same arbitrage stablecoins captured in payments.
insights.quote: Not calling each other to get a quote, not doing price discovery on Telegram, not paying ridiculous fees to intermediate agents, and not having ops teams in the global south moving funds around with email confirmations.

insights.claim: Schuermann frames Variational as the mirror image of stablecoins: where stablecoins moved fiat settlement, remittances and FX onchain and are displacing Fedwire and SWIFT, Variational aims to move derivative trading, settlement and clearing onchain.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: A clean analogy for sizing the opportunity: if stablecoin adoption is the template, derivatives settlement is the next comparable migration.

insights.claim: Schuermann says power and compute markets are becoming a new commodity complex with their own capital formation and product stack, and expects Variational to make moves in both markets on Omni and eventually Pro.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Signals a concrete roadmap direction toward power and compute derivatives onchain, and flags the recommodification theme for investors positioning around AI infrastructure.
insights.quote: We're watching kind of a recommodification of a new type of commodity.

insights.claim: Schuermann, whose research background is robotics including time at Google X, argues the market has gotten over its skis on near-term productionization of general-purpose robots, drawing the analogy to the early-2010s self-driving hype cycle that killed most entrants while Waymo survived.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: A caution on robotics valuations: expect booms, busts and consolidation before general-purpose deployment, even if the long-run thesis is right.
insights.quote: I think people have gotten a little bit over their skis in terms of thinking about how far we are along to productionizing these things.

insights.claim: Despite the near-term caution, Schuermann expects general-purpose robots to be deployed across all parts of the economy within a lifetime and probably in the near term in the grand scheme of things.
insights.speaker: Lucas Schuermann
insights.so_what: Separates the timing call from the terminal call, the standard structure for positioning through a hype-cycle drawdown.
insights.quote: we're going to have general purpose robots just everywhere in all parts of the economy
